hoy.titular: The day is here: the Pincha go for a fifth Libertadores

foto.alt: Estudiantes fans fill the stand at the UNO.

hoy.resumen: Estudiantes and Palmeiras decide the Cup today at 17:00 at the Centenario, with Fabricio Pérez replacing Baltasar Rodríguez. The coaches arrived overnight and more than 30,000 Pincha fans are expected in Montevideo.

siete.titulo: The day is here: the Pincha go for a fifth
siete.texto: Estudiantes and Palmeiras decide the Copa Libertadores in a one-off final at the Centenario, the same stadium and the same opponents as the 1968 final. If it is level, extra time and penalties; Jesús Valenzuela is the referee.

At his final press conference, the head coach thanked the fans for their support, which is "pure fuel for these matches", and said: "I believe strongly in our team, in our players". He singled out Palmeiras' individual quality, transitions and set pieces.

Fans from the 160 coaches arrived in the early hours after border delays: departure had been pushed back from 7:00 to 10:30 and most had only crossed by midnight. More than 30,000 Pincha fans are expected at the Centenario.

siete.titulo: Fabricio Pérez picked to fill Baltasar's place
siete.texto: In the last session in Montevideo, Medina lined up Muslera; Mancuso, Núñez, González Pírez and Rojo; Fabricio Pérez, Piovi, Castro and Tobio Burgos; Tiago Palacios and Carrillo. A back five with Gastón Benedetti remains an option, from the start or during the match.
Alexander Barboza, Palmeiras' Argentine defender, had claimed the Verdão will be champions. The Pincha captain replied with irony from Montevideo: "Congratulations on that..."

siete.titulo: Correa available, likely to start on the bench
siete.texto: Joaquín Correa trained alongside his team-mates after the tear he suffered against Flamengo and will be available to Medina as an option. He is expected to start the final among the substitutes.

siete.titulo: Win the Cup, reach the 2029 Club World Cup
siete.texto: As well as a fifth star, the final hands out a place at the 2029 Club World Cup: beat Palmeiras and the Pincha seal their ticket as champions of South America.

linea.texto: Almost USD 16 million in prize money so far, and how much more comes with the title.

Claudio Vivas, who discovered Carrillo and Rojo in the academy, will be cheering for the Pincha.
Medina previews the final: "Messages of support are pure fuel".
Carrillo hits back at Barboza, who claimed Palmeiras will be champions.
Hundreds of fans packed the Montevideo Fan Fest for a flag rally.
Medina: "Obviously there is no pressure in matches like this".
Pincha fans party on Pocitos beach.
A packed Fan Fest and a chanting duel with Palmeiras fans.
Palmeiras wrap up preparations with Murilo and Piquerez and settle two doubts.
Same stadium, same opponents, 58 years on: the Pincha go for a fifth.
The Pincha practised penalties with every scenario in mind, and goalkeeper Carlos Miguel.
The first fans arrive and Montevideo starts turning red and white.
